messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without making unsupported claims?

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without unsupported claims, the evidence must include formal R&S specifications / feature documents, official competitor documentation or third-party evidence, and AI-specific validation data such as benchmarks, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, test methodology, reproducibility data, and versioned configuration / option information; the current passages do not provide enough evidence for a direct, supported competitive AI comparison [9][21][24][26][30][33][35].
### Evidence required
| Evidence needed | Why it is required | Current support / gap |
|---|---|---|
| Formal R&S Signaling product evidence for CMX500, including specifications, features, software version, option codes, and stated limits | CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution for LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, signaling, TX measurements, WLAN signaling, fading, BLER, throughput, application testing, XLAPI, and SCPI, but its specifications and feature documents distinguish binding limits from non-binding or subject-to-change data.[7][8][9] | Use CMX500 specifications and features documents rather than sales battle cards for technical claims, because data without tolerance limits is not binding and feature overviews are not technical specifications datasheets.[9] |
| Formal R&S production / wireless communication device test evidence for CMP180, including measurement options and multiport architecture | CMP180 is documented as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing, configurable with RF generator/analyzer resources, measurement options, waveform options, and R&S VSE analysis capability.[10][11] | CMP180 claims should cite the CMP180 Features and Functions and Specifications documents, because the features document points users to the specifications document for measurement ranges and tolerance limits.[12] |
| Official competitor documentation or third-party evidence for every competitor capability claim | The CMX500 vs Keysight page states that competitor claims currently rely on an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Keysight official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[21] | The CMX500 vs Anritsu page states that Anritsu battle-card claims mainly come from an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Anritsu official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[24] |
| Same evidence rule for Amarisoft comparisons | The CMX500 vs Amarisoft page states that Amarisoft claims currently have only an R&S internal battle card as a single source and require Amarisoft official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[26] | “Only R&S” and “safe and future-proof choice” are sales language and should not be treated as verifiable technical specifications.[26] |
| AI-specific performance evidence for CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant | The AI Scripting Assistant is described as using generative AI and natural language processing to help generate, extend, and explain XLAPI scripts for CMX500, but the source provides no benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported script package list, or validation conditions.[28][30] | Claims such as “faster,” “more accurate,” “better coverage,” or “competitive advantage” for AI scripting would need benchmark results, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, supported package lists, and validation conditions that the current source does not provide.[30][33] |
| Formal AI product identity and availability evidence | The AI Scripting Assistant source does not provide formal product model, version, license code, order number, support contract, document version, availability date, deployment option types, supported LLM model, retrieval architecture, security controls, or update mechanism details.[33] | A customer-facing AI comparison would need those missing product, deployment, security, and version-control details before making implementation or availability claims.[33] |
| AI user-experience test methodology and reproducibility evidence | The China Mobile Research Institute / R&S generative AI testbed source says CMX500 can configure network parameters, fading models, latency, jitter, and RF impairments, and that KPIs include TTFT and TPS.[34] | The same source does not provide TTFT / TPS measurement methodology, prompt set, LLM model, server / cloud configuration, terminal model, radio scenario table, statistical treatment, reproducibility data, measured results, benchmark charts, or public report.[35] |
| Validation / certification evidence for conformance or operator-related claims | The CMX500 vs Keysight comparison lists NTN “first validated 3GPP NR-NTN RF + RRM + PCT with Samsung,” but also states that no validation report, PTCRB RFT 555 version, or test case list is provided.[92] | The Amarisoft battle-card page says claims about validated NR-NTN test cases with Samsung and PTCRB/GCF-aligned tests lack validation reports, test case lists, option codes, versions, and formal accreditation / certification documents.[47] |
| TCO / fewer-boxes / lower-cost evidence for commercial claims | CMX500 vs Keysight identifies “only platform,” “first validated,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” and “fewer boxes” as sales language, not verifiable technical specifications.[21] | CMX500 vs Anritsu says fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO, and higher throughput are sales messages, and the source provides no TCO formula.[94] |
| Configuration and test-setup evidence for Signaling solution notes | The Signaling test solution note says its CMX500 5G / Wi‑Fi configuration table lacks a formal configuration guide, software version, license bundle, quotation tool version, and release date.[37] | The same note says multi-technology De-sense validation lacks test cases, interference models, pass / fail limits, setup diagram, synchronization, shielding / chamber conditions, and automation flow.[37] |
| Clear separation between market mapping and formal product configuration | The AI server R&S solution mapping page says the Excel mapping is only a sales / test-solution clue and not a formal product configuration, customer relationship, or verified opportunity.[1] | The same mapping says R&S Solution fields are not formal datasheets, application notes, configuration guides, or ordering guides, and must not be used for quotation or formal test configuration.[63] |
### Minimum supported comparison package
| Comparison area | Minimum evidence to collect before making a claim | Passage basis |
|---|---|---|
| R&S Signaling capability | CMX500 specifications and feature documents with document version, software version, option codes, and binding limits.[7][9][71][72] | CMX500 has documented signaling and WLAN options, but binding claims must respect the specifications / feature-document limits.[7][9][71][72] |
| R&S Non-signaling capability | CMP200 / CMP180 specifications and feature documents with software versions, order numbers, measurement options, frequency / bandwidth conditions, and binding limits.[12][15][79][80] | CMP200 and CMP180 have documented non-signaling / production test roles and options, but their documents contain subject-to-change and non-binding-data limits.[12][15][79][80] |
| Competitor capability | Competitor official datasheets, product brochures, option guides, software-version documents, and third-party evidence for each competitor claim.[21][24][26] | R&S internal battle cards are sales positioning and cannot replace official competitor evidence.[19][21][22][24][25][26] |
| AI scripting comparison | Benchmarks, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, supported script package lists, validation conditions, product version, license code, deployment model, and security / update details.[30][33] | Current AI Scripting Assistant passages describe capabilities but do not provide those validation and product-boundary details.[30][33] |
| AI application experience testing | TTFT / TPS methodology, prompts, LLM model, server / cloud setup, terminal model, radio scenarios, statistics, reproducibility data, measured results, and benchmark reports.[34][35] | Current generative AI user-experience testbed passages list TTFT / TPS and CMX500-controlled network variables but do not provide methodology or measured benchmark data.[34][35] |
| Certification / operator claims | Validation reports, test case IDs, PTCRB / GCF versions, operator acceptance letters, scenario IDs, test-plan versions, and validation dates.[47][52][92] | Current passages explicitly note missing validation reports, test case lists, acceptance letters, scenario IDs, test-plan versions, and validation dates.[47][52][92] |
| Cost / TCO / productivity claims | TCO calculation basis, license counts, calibration costs, trade-in terms, test-time data, throughput data, or benchmark evidence.[45][47][94] | Current competitor passages say TCO and similar claims lack calculation basis, prices, license quantities, calibration-cost assumptions, or concrete commercial evidence.[45][47][94] |
### Unsupported claims to avoid unless the above evidence is collected
| Claim type to avoid | Why unsupported in current passages |
|---|---|
| “Our AI tester is better than the competitor’s AI solution.” | Current AI Scripting Assistant evidence lacks benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported package list, and validation conditions.[30] |
| “Our generative AI test solution produces superior TTFT / TPS results.” | The generative AI testbed source lists TTFT and TPS as KPIs but lacks methodology, prompt set, LLM model, configuration, statistical treatment, reproducibility data, measured data, benchmark charts, and public report.[34][35] |
| “Our solution has lower TCO or needs fewer boxes than the competitor.” | Lower TCO and fewer boxes are identified as sales language or sales messages, and the cited sources do not provide TCO calculations or cost assumptions.[21][94] |
| “Competitor X lacks capability Y.” | Keysight, Anritsu, and Amarisoft comparison pages say competitor claims from R&S internal battle cards require official competitor data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[21][24][26] |
| “The AI server mapping proves customer fit or a formal configuration.” | The AI server solution mapping is a sales / test-solution clue only and is not a formal product configuration, customer relationship, verified opportunity, datasheet, application note, configuration guide, or ordering guide.[1][63] |

R&S CMP200 › Product data 使用限制
依 [[CMP200_specs_en_5216-4391-22_v0800]]：

- Product data 適用條件為 ambient temperature 儲存 3 小時後 warm-up operation 30 分鐘、符合指定 environmental conditions、遵守 recommended calibration interval，且如適用需完成 all internal automatic adjustments。
- Specifications with limits 代表保證的 product performance，以 `<`、`≤`、`>`、`≥`、`±`、maximum、limit of、minimum 等形式標示。
- Non-traceable specifications with limits（n. trc.）依 limits 測試，但因 measuring equipment 不可追溯至 national metrology standards，Rohde & Schwarz 不保證其 performance。
- Typical data（typ.）、nominal values（nom.）、measured values（meas.）均不由 Rohde & Schwarz 保證。
- Uncertainties 採 coverage factor 2，依 GUM 計算。
- 3GPP 標準中 chip rates 以 Mcps 表示，bit rates / symbol rates 以 Gbps、Mbps、kbps、Msps、ksps 表示，sample rates 以 Msample/s 表示；這些不是 SI units。

R&S CMP200 › 產品定位
依 [[CMP200_specs_en_5216-4391-22_v0800]]，[[R&S CMP200]] 與 [[R&S CMPHEAD30]] / [[R&S CMPHEAD50]] remote radio head（RRH）形成 5G NR FR2（mmWave）nonsignaling one-box test solution，目標應用為：

- R&D 的 RF parametric testing。
- Manufacturing 的 high-volume RF parametric testing。
- Fully assembled smart devices 的 pure radiated mmWave setup。
- 具 IF interface 的 mmWave RF integrated circuits 的 mixed radiated mmWave / conducted IF setup。
- 具 mmWave interface 的 mmWave RF integrated circuits 的 mixed radiated mmWave / conducted mmWave setup。

R&S CMX500 vs Keysight › R&S offensive plays
依 [[2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card]]：

- **One-Box FR1 + FR2 + WLAN + Fading + IP + NTN + RedCap**：將 [[R&S CMX500]] 定位為 unified system；對比 Keysight 需要 E7515P / E7515B / E7515E、E7515W、E7515R、RaySim / Channel Studio 與 additional tools。
- **FR2 / NTN Conformance Leadership**：主張 CMX500 有 50 GHz mmWave (RRH evo)、FR2 maturity、first validated 3GPP NR-NTN conformance with Samsung、RedCap via OBT-Lite。
- **WLAN in Every Configuration**：主張 CMX500 可在每個 configuration 中整合 Wi-Fi 6 / 6E / 7 signaling；對比 Keysight Wi-Fi 只在 E7515W 或 E7515P。
- **FR3 / 6G on One Platform**：主張 CMX500 可透過 [[RFU18]] 與 6G-relevant testing 演進，包含 AI-CSI feedback、satellite Doppler、NTN mobility、FR3 channel models；對比 Keysight multi-component approach。
- **Unified Automation**：將 CMsquares、CMsequencer、CONTEST、AI Script Assistant 定位為 one unified environment；對比 Atlas、Channel Studio、RaySim、WLAN-specific tools、Nemo、UXM-specific application features。
- **Simplify the Message**：以 fewer boxes、fewer SKUs、more capability、lower TCO 作為 sales headline。

R&S CMX500 vs Keysight › Sales landmines
[[2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card]] 建議用以下問題區分需求：

1. 要覆蓋 FR1、FR2、Wi-Fi 7、RedCap 與 NTN 時，需要多少 UXM models，且誰負責 integration？
2. 是否需要 integrated fading、Doppler 與 satellite mobility in one box，或能接受 RaySim / Channel Studio / ProbSim 等 external tools？
3. 是否需要 one unified automation environment，而不是 six separate tools？
4. 是否需要 Wi-Fi 6 / 6E / 7 on every test configuration？
5. 是否需要 validated 3GPP NR-NTN conformance（RF + RRM + PCT）with ecosystem partner，以因應 operator 或 certification pressure？
6. 轉向 FR3 時，是否要 upgrade same platform（例如 add an RF unit），或導入 new boxes and new software？
7. RedCap testing 是否要在 main 5G signaling tester 中，或能接受 separate RedCap-only box？
8. Operators 或 certification bodies 是否要求 specific timeline 上的 validated NR-NTN conformance？
9. 團隊需要學習與維護多少不同 software environments，且 tool updates 是否會破壞 automation？

R&S CMX500 vs Keysight › 矛盾與限制
⚠️ [[2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card]]（2026-02-26）說 quick comparison table 中 [[R&S CMX500]] cellular FR1 up to **18 GHz**、FR2 up to **50 GHz (RRH evo)**，但既有頁面 [[R&S CMX500]] 依 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]] 說 [[R&S CMX-B600B]] RF unit frequency range **400 MHz to 8000 MHz**，[[R&S CMX-B500A]] IF generator **6 GHz to 20 GHz**、IF analyzer **4 GHz to 20 GHz**，FR2 remote radio heads 為 [[R&S CMXHEAD30]] / [[R&S CMXHEAD50]] / [[R&S CMXHEAD50-Evo]]。判斷：battle card quick table 不能取代正式 specifications；FR1 up to 18 GHz 需視為 RFU18 / FR3 roadmap sales wording。

⚠️ [[2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card]]（2026-02-26）說 [[RFU18]] 提供 max aggregated NR bandwidth **2000 MHz**，但既有頁面 [[R&S CMX500]] 依 [[CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100]] 說 [[R&S CMX-B600B]] RF bandwidth **250 MHz**、[[R&S CMX-B500A]] IF analyzer bandwidth up to **1 GHz**，且 [[CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32]] 說 IF unit 最高 **800 MHz total carrier bandwidth**、NR FR2 channel bandwidth **50 / 100 / 200 / 400 MHz**。判斷：2000 MHz 屬 RFU18 / roadmap sales claim，不可回填為既有 CMX500 binding specification。

R&S CMX500 vs Keysight › 核心 thesis
依 [[2026_02_CMX500_Keysight_Sales_Battle_Card]]（2026-02-26），R&S 對 Keysight 的核心定位是：[[R&S CMX500]] 提供 one-platform integration，涵蓋 cellular FR1 / FR2 / FR3 path、Wi-Fi、fading、IP/application testing、NTN、RedCap、RF analysis 與 signaling；相對地，Keysight 被描述為依賴 multiple UXM SKUs、add-on software 與 external tools。

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › R&S offensive plays
依 [[2026_02_CMX500_Anritsu_Sales_Battle_Card]]：

- **One-Box FR1 + FR2 + FR3 + WLAN + Fading + IP**：將 [[R&S CMX500]] 定位為 unified system，對比 Anritsu 的 MT8000A、MT8862A、IP Option 012 + external PC、external fading chambers 與 separate RF boards。
- **FR2 / FR3 performance leadership**：主張 R&S up to 50 GHz FR2、>16 GHz instantaneous bandwidth、>10 Gbps data rates 與 FR3 via RFU18；使用時需加註非正式規格限制。
- **Integrated WLAN signaling**：主張 R&S Wi-Fi 6 / 6E / 7 signaling directly inside CMX500，Anritsu 需 separate MT8862A。
- **R&D → Conformance → Production**：CMX500、CMW500、CMP180、CMP200、CMW100 構成 one vendor / one workflow / full lifecycle。
- **Future-proof technology**：Validated NTN、ORAN ORU / Conformance with partners、FR3 beyond 16 GHz、RedCap Rel-17/18。
- **Unified software ecosystem**：R&S Test Automation Suite 與 unified user experience；對比 Anritsu SSNR、RTD、ATS、MX844030PC。此項與 [[mx844030pc-j1200]] 對 MX844030PC common RTD GUI 的說明並列保留，使用時需標明來源層次。
- **Fewer Boxes. More Capability.**：以 fewer calibrations、fewer licenses、lower TCO、higher test throughput 作為 sales message；來源未提供 TCO 算式。

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › Sales landmines
[[2026_02_CMX500_Anritsu_Sales_Battle_Card]] 建議用以下問題區分需求：

1. 是否需要 FR1 bandwidth beyond 400 MHz，例如 600–800 MHz per carrier for 5G-Advanced Rel-18 / Rel-19 testing？
2. 是否需要 FR1、FR2、FR3、WLAN 與 LTE 在 single instrument 中且不用 hardware swaps？
3. 是否需要 native fading with high-throughput IP testing？
4. 是否偏好 one unified software platform，而不是 four separate tools？
5. 是否需要 advanced CA 或 mobility without adding extra boxes？
6. 是否需要 FR3 testing beyond 16 GHz，以支援 emerging 6G FR3 evaluations？

R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu › 與 Anritsu MX844030PC 官方 brochure 的關係
[[mx844030pc-j1200]]（2026-02-10）是 Anritsu 對 [[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 的 product brochure，確認 MX844030PC 為 **Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software**，支援 MAC-IF、PHY-IF Digital-IQ 與 RF-IF for RedCap，並使用 common [[RTD]] GUI 連接 Pre-silicon / Post-silicon protocol testing workflow。

⚠️ 來源 [[mx844030pc-j1200]]（2026-02-10）說 [[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 使用 common [[RTD]] GUI，讓 NR protocol test cases 可在 Post-Silicon 與 Pre-silicon phase 間移植，但既有頁面 [[R&S CMX500 vs Anritsu]] 說 Anritsu software 為 SSNR + RTD + ATS + MX844030PC 的 fragmented / disconnected tools。判斷：官方 brochure 支撐 MX844030PC 與 RTD 有整合面；battle card 的 fragmented 判斷仍可作為 R&S sales positioning，但不得當作 Anritsu 官方規格描述。

### Short answer
To compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without unsupported claims, the evidence must include formal R&S specifications / feature documents, official competitor documentation or third-party evidence, and AI-specific validation data such as benchmarks, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, test methodology, reproducibility data, and versioned configuration / option information; the current passages do not provide enough evidence for a direct, supported competitive AI comparison [9][21][24][26][30][33][35].
### Evidence required
| Evidence needed | Why it is required | Current support / gap |
|---|---|---|
| Formal R&S Signaling product evidence for CMX500, including specifications, features, software version, option codes, and stated limits | CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution for LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, TDD, signaling, TX measurements, WLAN signaling, fading, BLER, throughput, application testing, XLAPI, and SCPI, but its specifications and feature documents distinguish binding limits from non-binding or subject-to-change data.[7][8][9] | Use CMX500 specifications and features documents rather than sales battle cards for technical claims, because data without tolerance limits is not binding and feature overviews are not technical specifications datasheets.[9] |
| Formal R&S production / wireless communication device test evidence for CMP180, including measurement options and multiport architecture | CMP180 is documented as a Radio Communication Tester for production / wireless communication device testing, configurable with RF generator/analyzer resources, measurement options, waveform options, and R&S VSE analysis capability.[10][11] | CMP180 claims should cite the CMP180 Features and Functions and Specifications documents, because the features document points users to the specifications document for measurement ranges and tolerance limits.[12] |
| Official competitor documentation or third-party evidence for every competitor capability claim | The CMX500 vs Keysight page states that competitor claims currently rely on an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Keysight official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[21] | The CMX500 vs Anritsu page states that Anritsu battle-card claims mainly come from an R&S internal battle card and should be checked against Anritsu official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[24] |
| Same evidence rule for Amarisoft comparisons | The CMX500 vs Amarisoft page states that Amarisoft claims currently have only an R&S internal battle card as a single source and require Amarisoft official data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[26] | “Only R&S” and “safe and future-proof choice” are sales language and should not be treated as verifiable technical specifications.[26] |
| AI-specific performance evidence for CMX500 AI Scripting Assistant | The AI Scripting Assistant is described as using generative AI and natural language processing to help generate, extend, and explain XLAPI scripts for CMX500, but the source provides no benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported script package list, or validation conditions.[28][30] | Claims such as “faster,” “more accurate,” “better coverage,” or “competitive advantage” for AI scripting would need benchmark results, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, supported package lists, and validation conditions that the current source does not provide.[30][33] |
| Formal AI product identity and availability evidence | The AI Scripting Assistant source does not provide formal product model, version, license code, order number, support contract, document version, availability date, deployment option types, supported LLM model, retrieval architecture, security controls, or update mechanism details.[33] | A customer-facing AI comparison would need those missing product, deployment, security, and version-control details before making implementation or availability claims.[33] |
| AI user-experience test methodology and reproducibility evidence | The China Mobile Research Institute / R&S generative AI testbed source says CMX500 can configure network parameters, fading models, latency, jitter, and RF impairments, and that KPIs include TTFT and TPS.[34] | The same source does not provide TTFT / TPS measurement methodology, prompt set, LLM model, server / cloud configuration, terminal model, radio scenario table, statistical treatment, reproducibility data, measured results, benchmark charts, or public report.[35] |
| Validation / certification evidence for conformance or operator-related claims | The CMX500 vs Keysight comparison lists NTN “first validated 3GPP NR-NTN RF + RRM + PCT with Samsung,” but also states that no validation report, PTCRB RFT 555 version, or test case list is provided.[92] | The Amarisoft battle-card page says claims about validated NR-NTN test cases with Samsung and PTCRB/GCF-aligned tests lack validation reports, test case lists, option codes, versions, and formal accreditation / certification documents.[47] |
| TCO / fewer-boxes / lower-cost evidence for commercial claims | CMX500 vs Keysight identifies “only platform,” “first validated,” “leadership,” “lower TCO,” and “fewer boxes” as sales language, not verifiable technical specifications.[21] | CMX500 vs Anritsu says fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO, and higher throughput are sales messages, and the source provides no TCO formula.[94] |
| Configuration and test-setup evidence for Signaling solution notes | The Signaling test solution note says its CMX500 5G / Wi‑Fi configuration table lacks a formal configuration guide, software version, license bundle, quotation tool version, and release date.[37] | The same note says multi-technology De-sense validation lacks test cases, interference models, pass / fail limits, setup diagram, synchronization, shielding / chamber conditions, and automation flow.[37] |
| Clear separation between market mapping and formal product configuration | The AI server R&S solution mapping page says the Excel mapping is only a sales / test-solution clue and not a formal product configuration, customer relationship, or verified opportunity.[1] | The same mapping says R&S Solution fields are not formal datasheets, application notes, configuration guides, or ordering guides, and must not be used for quotation or formal test configuration.[63] |
### Minimum supported comparison package
| Comparison area | Minimum evidence to collect before making a claim | Passage basis |
|---|---|---|
| R&S Signaling capability | CMX500 specifications and feature documents with document version, software version, option codes, and binding limits.[7][9][71][72] | CMX500 has documented signaling and WLAN options, but binding claims must respect the specifications / feature-document limits.[7][9][71][72] |
| R&S Non-signaling capability | CMP200 / CMP180 specifications and feature documents with software versions, order numbers, measurement options, frequency / bandwidth conditions, and binding limits.[12][15][79][80] | CMP200 and CMP180 have documented non-signaling / production test roles and options, but their documents contain subject-to-change and non-binding-data limits.[12][15][79][80] |
| Competitor capability | Competitor official datasheets, product brochures, option guides, software-version documents, and third-party evidence for each competitor claim.[21][24][26] | R&S internal battle cards are sales positioning and cannot replace official competitor evidence.[19][21][22][24][25][26] |
| AI scripting comparison | Benchmarks, correctness metrics, coverage matrices, supported script package lists, validation conditions, product version, license code, deployment model, and security / update details.[30][33] | Current AI Scripting Assistant passages describe capabilities but do not provide those validation and product-boundary details.[30][33] |
| AI application experience testing | TTFT / TPS methodology, prompts, LLM model, server / cloud setup, terminal model, radio scenarios, statistics, reproducibility data, measured results, and benchmark reports.[34][35] | Current generative AI user-experience testbed passages list TTFT / TPS and CMX500-controlled network variables but do not provide methodology or measured benchmark data.[34][35] |
| Certification / operator claims | Validation reports, test case IDs, PTCRB / GCF versions, operator acceptance letters, scenario IDs, test-plan versions, and validation dates.[47][52][92] | Current passages explicitly note missing validation reports, test case lists, acceptance letters, scenario IDs, test-plan versions, and validation dates.[47][52][92] |
| Cost / TCO / productivity claims | TCO calculation basis, license counts, calibration costs, trade-in terms, test-time data, throughput data, or benchmark evidence.[45][47][94] | Current competitor passages say TCO and similar claims lack calculation basis, prices, license quantities, calibration-cost assumptions, or concrete commercial evidence.[45][47][94] |
### Unsupported claims to avoid unless the above evidence is collected
| Claim type to avoid | Why unsupported in current passages |
|---|---|
| “Our AI tester is better than the competitor’s AI solution.” | Current AI Scripting Assistant evidence lacks benchmark, correctness metric, coverage matrix, supported package list, and validation conditions.[30] |
| “Our generative AI test solution produces superior TTFT / TPS results.” | The generative AI testbed source lists TTFT and TPS as KPIs but lacks methodology, prompt set, LLM model, configuration, statistical treatment, reproducibility data, measured data, benchmark charts, and public report.[34][35] |
| “Our solution has lower TCO or needs fewer boxes than the competitor.” | Lower TCO and fewer boxes are identified as sales language or sales messages, and the cited sources do not provide TCO calculations or cost assumptions.[21][94] |
| “Competitor X lacks capability Y.” | Keysight, Anritsu, and Amarisoft comparison pages say competitor claims from R&S internal battle cards require official competitor data and third-party evidence for customer documents.[21][24][26] |
| “The AI server mapping proves customer fit or a formal configuration.” | The AI server solution mapping is a sales / test-solution clue only and is not a formal product configuration, customer relationship, verified opportunity, datasheet, application note, configuration guide, or ordering guide.[1][63] |
